items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was gigging with Dexter and Wardell; they had a group, two tenors and a trumpet... Wardell got a chance to make a recording for Prestige Records, and he asked me to do it with him.

ctx.x: McShann being from Kansas City at that.

Yeah, it’s all education. It’s a school. Life is a school. I got out there, [and] by that time, I knew a little more about playing, so I was able to get jobs with people like Gerald Wilson and Benny Carter, Wardell Gray, Teddy Edwards, good players.
When did you join the McShann band, and when did you leave New York?
